# When you can withdraw your super

The conditions of release that must be satisfied for legal superannuation withdrawals.

**Last updated** 10 July 2026

Print or Download

## On this page

- [Conditions of super release](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#ato-Conditionsofsuperrelease)
- [Accessing your super early](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#ato-Accessingyoursuperearly)
- [Illegal early access schemes](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#ato-Illegalearlyaccessschemes)

## Conditions of super release

You can withdraw your super when **any of the following apply**:

- You turn 65 years old, even if you're still working.
- You reach your preservation age and choose to [retire](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#Whatisretirement).
- You reach your preservation age, continue working, and start a [transition to retirement income stream](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/retirement-withdrawal-lump-sum-or-income-stream).
- You meet a condition that allows early access to your super.

### Retirement

Retirement means you have ceased **paid employment** either:

- when you were 60 years old or over
- before you turned 60 years old **and** you have reached your [preservation age](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#Preservationage).

Your superannuation fund must be satisfied you have no intention of becoming employed again in the future.

Learn more about options for withdrawing your super when you retire – see [Retirement withdrawal – lump sum or income stream](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/retirement-withdrawal-lump-sum-or-income-stream).

### Preservation age

Your preservation age is **not the same** as your pension age. Check with [Services AustraliaExternal Link](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/individuals/services/centrelink/age-pension/who-can-get-it) for the rules about accessing an age pension.

Your preservation age is the age at which you can access your super if you're either retired or you have started a transition to retirement income stream.

Your preservation age depends on when you were born, as shown in this table.

| Date of birth | Preservation age (years) |
| --- | --- |
| Before 1 July 1960 | 55 |
| 1 July 1960 – 30 June 1961 | 56 |
| 1 July 1961 – 30 June 1962 | 57 |
| 1 July 1962 – 30 June 1963 | 58 |
| 1 July 1963 – 30 June 1964 | 59 |
| From 1 July 1964 | 60 |

Preservation age based on date of birth

### After your death

If a person dies, in most cases their super fund pays their remaining super interest to their nominated beneficiary.

Super that is paid after a person's death is called a [super death benefit](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/superannuation-death-benefits).

## Accessing your super early

In very limited circumstances, you can access your super early.

These circumstances include:

- [medical, compassionate, hardship and incapacity grounds](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/early-access-to-super/when-you-can-access-your-super-early)
- accessing your **voluntary contributions** through the [First Home Super Saver scheme](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/early-access-to-super/first-home-super-saver-scheme)
- being a [temporary resident](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/temporary-residents-and-superannuation/how-superannuation-applies-to-temporary-residents) who is leaving Australia
- having a **low super balance**, such as a

  - [super account balance of less than $200](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/early-access-to-super/when-you-can-access-your-super-early#ato-Superbalancelessthan200) after your employment is terminated
  - [lost super account](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/growing-and-keeping-track-of-your-super/keeping-track-of-your-super/ato-held-super) with a balance of **less than $200**.

## Illegal early access schemes

It is illegal to withdraw your super unless you satisfy a [condition of release](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/super-withdrawal-options#Conditionsofreleaseofsuper).

Beware of people promoting early-access to super schemes. Participating in [illegal early access schemes](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/early-access-to-super/illegal-early-access-to-super) will cost you a lot more than the super you withdraw.
